answer: Hardware-rooted personhood: every agent anchors its identity to a unique secure-enclave key burned into physical silicon at manufacture, so a sybil farmer cannot mint a fresh vertex without owning another machine. The enclave signs each action as a verifiable signal, and peers score an agent history like critics weighing a sonnet - every line traceable to one unforgeable device. Cloning software copies nothing but an empty shell; the vertex of trust lives in hardware no copy can reproduce, so each fake identity costs real manufacturing, not a keystroke.
